answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents stake capital in a trust network modeled like a flow graph. Game-theoretic multi-agent auditing enforces topological cut verifications across transaction channels: legitimate throughput streams like an ocean, while sparse attacker bottlenecks dry down to an isolated river. When adversarial audits detect fictitious clusters, stake slashing burns fraudulent deposits, pushing the adversary payoff to a complete nadir and scaling attacker cost superlinearly with cluster size.
